lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Experience is not presented newest-first because Harbor Payments appears below the older Crestline Logistics role.
items.because: The current ordering makes a 2024 product internship look older than a role that ended in 2023.

items.says: The product-management direction is diluted by giving Coastal Marine Services a full multi-bullet entry.
items.because: The marine mechanic role is the page's most obvious unrelated experience for a product-management target.

items.says: Education appears before the professional experience that should carry the page.
items.because: The candidate has five years of professional experience and a completed MBA, so leading with education understates the work history.

items.says: The product-management project evidence is separated from the relevant internship by the education section.
items.because: The internship and Campus Food Rescue App together show the clearest product direction, but their separation weakens that narrative.

items.says: The current-role bullets use past-tense verbs instead of present tense.
items.because: The role is current, so 'Rebuilt' and 'keeping' suggest the work has ended or mix incompatible tenses.

items.says: The dry-dock threshold has no baseline, change, or comparison.
items.because: A reader can see that jobs were completed in under five days but cannot judge whether that was faster than the prior process or standard for the work.

items.says: The current-role verbs 'Maintained' and 'logged' should be present tense.
items.because: Past-tense verbs conflict with the listed Present role and can make ongoing maintenance and recordkeeping sound historical.

items.says: The inspection-purpose phrase gives no resulting outcome from the maintenance or records.
items.because: Preparing for an inspection is a purpose, not an outcome.

items.says: The carrier scorecard and review responsibility has no stated resulting change or decision.
items.because: A hiring reader can see the recurring responsibility but cannot tell whether it improved carrier performance, resolved service problems, or enabled management action.

items.says: 'Owned the weekly carrier scorecards' frames the work as a responsibility rather than an action performed.
items.because: The wording tells the reader what was assigned to the candidate but not what the candidate did with the information.

items.says: The monthly review meeting is described passively and does not name the candidate's action.
items.because: The phrase makes the meeting sound like an event that merely occurred rather than one the candidate led or used to drive decisions.

items.says: The 30% reduction in warehouse pick errors has no baseline error rate or measurement period.
items.because: The percentage establishes a reduction, but a reader cannot judge the size or comparability of the result without knowing what it was measured against.

items.says: The line does not define what 'forecast error' measures or the evaluation period.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether the figures use the same error metric and comparable forecasting windows.

items.says: The S&OP bullet repeats its cadence and duration.
items.because: Calling the review quarterly and then adding 12 consecutive quarters uses two phrases to establish related timing.

items.says: The route-planning tool is not described in terms of the planning capability or operational change it introduced.
items.because: A reader can see that implementation work occurred, but cannot tell what contribution drove the efficiency gain.

items.says: The 1,800 annual driver-hour savings has no stated baseline or calculation basis.
items.because: The annual total communicates scale, but a reader cannot assess whether it came from a before-and-after comparison, modeled routes, or another basis.

items.says: The route-planning bullet uses a long list of methods that obscures the main achievement.
items.because: Several process details appear before the savings result, so the reader must work through them to find the impact.

items.says: The strongest result appears only after an overlong process description.
items.because: The reader encounters several methods before learning what changed.

items.says: 'Taking over vendor negotiations' is informal and does not clearly identify the action performed.
items.because: The phrase sounds like a transfer of responsibility rather than a defined negotiation contribution.

items.says: The past-tense action sequence is weakened by the gerund 'shipping it.'
items.because: The bullet begins with completed actions, then shifts to a different construction for the final step.

items.says: The RICE Reach score is misused as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
items.because: RICE Reach is the number of people, customers, transactions, or other defined units affected during a specified period.

items.says: The line says the dispute roadmap was prioritized but does not state what the prioritization changed or achieved.
items.because: The framework shows process, but a hiring reader cannot see the value of the decision or the problem it addressed.

items.says: 'RICE' is unexplained jargon for readers outside product teams.
items.because: A recruiter may not know that it is a prioritization framework.

items.says: The line gives no evidence that the Reach scoring led to a measurable result.
items.because: Even a correctly applied prioritization framework does not show whether it improved a decision or outcome.

items.says: The roadmap priority is not connected to what it enabled or changed.
items.because: The reader can see that a decision was made, but not why it mattered to Harbor Payments or its merchants.

items.says: The phrase 'sizing the loss by segment' does not state the size of the loss or its comparison.
items.because: Without one anchor, the analysis sounds thorough but its decision value cannot be judged.

items.says: The roadmap outcome is buried after a long list of research and planning methods.
items.because: The reader reaches the important decision only after several process details.

items.says: The session-level test result is reported as an effect on merchants' customers.
items.because: Randomization by session estimates conversion differences per session, not automatically the effect on individual customers or merchants.

items.says: The wording obscures what metric actually improved in the checkout test.
items.because: The phrase makes the lift sound like a general effect on people rather than a measured conversion result.

items.says: The leadership funding and regional rollout do not show the result or comparison behind the decision.
items.because: Funding and expansion are credible consequences, but regions measure reach rather than what the onboarding work improved.

items.says: 'A follow-up roadmap' is vague and adds little beyond 'roadmap.'
items.because: The phrase does not tell the reader what was presented or how it differed from the onboarding results.

items.says: The checkout experiment and its five-point lift are repeated in two bullets.
items.because: Both lines describe the same experiment, so the internship appears to contain less distinct product work than it does.

items.says: The two dispute-roadmap bullets overlap by describing the same prioritization work through different methods.
items.because: One bullet emphasizes RICE and the other emphasizes research and the business case, but both culminate in roadmap prioritization.

items.says: The internship reads as two overlapping workstreams, with duplicate reporting of the checkout result.
items.because: The checkout optimization and dispute-roadmap work are both relevant, but the repeated experiment result blurs the distinction between them.

items.says: The line says 'Launched a surplus-food pickup app' but does not say what product or operating work the candidate performed.
items.because: A reader can see the outcome but cannot tell what the Product Lead actually built, coordinated, or introduced.

items.says: 'that would have been thrown away' is passive and adds words without clarifying the result.
items.because: The passive construction puts attention on a hypothetical disposal event rather than the food rescued.

items.says: 'with two dining halls' is awkwardly attached and does not clearly say whether the app served those halls or was launched in partnership with them.
items.because: A recruiter may not know whether the dining halls were customers, operating sites, or launch partners.

items.says: The claim that weekly active users rose from 400 to 1,150 is a 187.5% increase, not a 150% increase.
items.because: The increase is 750 users, and 750 divided by the original 400 equals 187.5%.

items.says: The 60 interviews do not establish that pickup reminders caused weekly active users to rise from 400 to 1,150.
items.because: Interviews can inform feature selection, but they cannot demonstrate the feature's causal effect on usage.

items.says: The line does not state the comparison period or endpoint date for the increase in weekly active users.
items.because: A reader can see the size of the change but not how quickly it occurred or whether both figures were measured on comparable terms.

items.says: The line does not show what the 60 user interviews revealed.
items.because: The interviews establish research activity, but the reader cannot see how the research informed the product decision.

items.says: The rise from 75% to 95% is 20 percentage points, not a 20% increase.
items.because: The relative increase is approximately 26.7%, while the absolute change is 20 percentage points.

items.says: Setting up a volunteer shift system does not by itself establish that the system caused the fill rate to rise from 75% to 95%.
items.because: The intervention is a plausible way to improve slot coverage, but the before-and-after change could also reflect other concurrent changes.

items.says: The $2.4M annual saving is not identified as projected, modeled, or realized.
items.because: A hiring reader needs to distinguish an estimate used to justify a pilot from savings already captured.

items.says: The line names the scheduling change but not how the candidate produced the estimate.
items.because: The reader can see the proposed consolidation, but not the analysis or assumptions behind the figure.

items.says: The adopted intake changes have no stated operational or patient result.
items.because: Adoption shows that front-desk staff accepted the recommendation, not whether it improved intake, reduced effort, or changed the patient experience.

items.says: The line does not specify how much the intake form was shortened or what it was measured against.
items.because: The reader cannot judge the scale of the change from the statement alone.

items.says: The passive intake sentence hides who performed the mapping and shortening.
items.because: A reader can see that the work happened but cannot tell what the candidate personally did.

items.says: The implementation result is buried in a passive trailing clause.
items.because: The reader reaches staff adoption only after the process description, and the sentence does not clearly connect the candidate to the result.

items.says: The line says the final recommendation was presented but not how it was developed or supported.
items.because: A reader can see that the candidate reached decision-makers, but not what consulting skill produced a recommendation they approved.

items.says: The important pilot-approval result appears only after the presentation method and audience.
items.because: The approval is the strongest evidence of influence, but the current order makes it feel secondary to presenting.

items.says: The consulting bullets repeat the client approval or funding of a scheduling pilot.
items.because: Both bullets report the same downstream decision, so the practicum appears to have fewer distinct results.
